headline: Trump, Xi and Putin to hold unprecedented joint meeting in China
standfirst: The leaders of the US, China and Russia are planning an unprecedented joint meeting during the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
keyPoints: US, Chinese and Russian leaders will hold a trilateral meeting in Shenzhen.
Discussions will focus on nuclear weapons reduction and the war in Iran.
The meeting will exclude talks on Russia's war in Ukraine.
No formal agreements or joint statements are expected from the summit.

paragraphs: The leaders of the United States, China and Russia are planning an unprecedented joint meeting on the sidelines of an international economic summit next week. White House officials confirmed that Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin will gather for three-way talks in the southern Chinese technology hub of Shenzhen. The historic gathering will take place during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit, which brings together 21 member economies in the region.

US officials indicated that the agenda for the upcoming trilateral session will focus primarily on the reduction of global nuclear arsenals and the ongoing war in Iran. Washington representatives stated that the American president intends to address the dangers of nuclear proliferation with his counterparts. However, officials clarified that the separate conflict in Ukraine will not be part of the discussions during this specific meeting.

The announcement follows a series of diplomatic visits between the three nations over the course of the year. While the three heads of state have frequently interacted in bilateral formats, a joint meeting of this nature represents a novel diplomatic milestone. White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales confirmed the itinerary to reporters following statements from Russian and Chinese officials regarding readiness for talks.

sections.heading: Historical context and diplomatic background
paragraphs: The planned gathering recalls the 1945 Yalta summit where Allied leaders laid out post-war settlements and territorial boundaries. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy has voiced concern that the Shenzhen talks could resemble a modern redistribution of spheres of influence. The Trump administration has maintained that separate negotiation tracks already exist for resolving the conflict in Ukraine without involving Beijing.

The meeting occurs against the backdrop of a lapsed nuclear arms control pact between Washington and Moscow that previously capped their atomic stockpiles. The United States has expressed a desire to replace the expired treaty with a broader framework that includes China. Beijing currently maintains a significantly smaller nuclear arsenal than either the US or Russia and has shown limited interest in joining such a pact.

sections.heading: Perspectives from participating nations
paragraphs: Analysts suggest that Beijing may view the summit as an opportunity to project its growing international influence and economic prestige. Hosting the world's most powerful nuclear states in an ultramodern coastal metropolis allows China to showcase its rapid technological and urban development. Yet some experts note the gathering could complicate Beijing's portrayal of itself as a neutral defender of multilateral free trade.

For the Kremlin, the trilateral format offers a valued chance to project superpower status alongside Washington and Beijing. Moscow has increasingly relied on trade ties with China following Western sanctions related to the conflict in Ukraine. Meanwhile, the US president aims to secure strategic discussions on nuclear non-proliferation and Middle Eastern security despite low expectations for immediate breakthroughs.

sections.heading: Global implications and regional reactions
paragraphs: The high-profile summit risks overshadowing the broader economic discussions at the multi-day APEC gathering in Shenzhen. Observers point out that symbolism will likely outweigh substantive policy outcomes, with no formal joint agreements anticipated by participating delegations. The visual of the three leaders conferring together carries immense geopolitical weight for international relations.

Regional observers remain watchful of how the trilateral dynamics might influence broader security arrangements in the Indo-Pacific and beyond. While Washington pursues cooperation on arms control, tensions persist across various trade and technological fronts. European capitals have also monitored shifting diplomatic alignments with caution as major powers realign their strategic priorities.

sections.heading: Upcoming schedule and future outlook
paragraphs: President Trump is scheduled to depart Washington early in the week and will first attend an Association of South-east Asian Nations summit in the Philippines. He will then travel to China to arrive in Shenzhen ahead of the multi-nation economic conference. Alongside the trilateral talks, the US leader will hold a bilateral working meeting with the Chinese president.

Following the conclusion of the summit events in China, the participating governments are expected to evaluate the outcomes of the high-level exchanges. Whether the historic meeting creates a foundation for future arms control negotiations remains uncertain. Analysts emphasize that ongoing diplomatic channels will continue to dictate relations between the world's leading nuclear powers.

highlight: The historic meeting between the respective leaders of the US, Russia and China will take place as Trump attends the Asia-Pacific Economic Co-operation summit.
socialSummary: US, China and Russia plan an unprecedented trilateral meeting in Shenzhen to discuss nuclear arms and regional security.
